content.title: How to Collect SMS Opt-In
content.summary: Before you can text your contacts, they need to clearly agree to it. This guide shows you exactly what a compliant opt-in looks like with a real example form and a simple checklist.

sections.heading: The Compliant Web Form
sections.body: Here is what a fully compliant SMS opt-in form looks like. Every element below is a carrier requirement. Use this Brightside Pest Control example as the model for your own signup page.

rows.label: ☐ Service updates
rows.value: Text me service and appointment updates from Brightside Pest Control

rows.label: ☐ Deals & promos
rows.value: Text me deals and promotions from Brightside Pest Control

rows.label: ☐ Terms & Privacy
rows.value: I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy

rows.label: Fine print
rows.value: Consent not required. Msg & data rates apply. Frequency varies. Reply STOP / HELP.

sections.heading: Split the Consent
sections.body: If you send both transactional messages (reminders, account notices) and marketing messages (promotions, offers), you cannot cover them with one checkbox. Each type needs its own, plus a separate Terms acknowledgment.

rows.label: Transactional SMS
rows.value: Appointment and account texts with frequency and rate disclosures

rows.label: Marketing SMS
rows.value: Offers and promotions, plus "consent is not a condition of purchase"

rows.label: Terms & Privacy
rows.value: "I accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" with links

sidebar.heading: Every opt-in must include

facts.label: 4. Message types
facts.value: Describe what texts they will get

sidebar.callout_text: A single checkbox covering all SMS types, or wording like "by submitting this form you agree to receive texts," will fail carrier review. Keep message types on separate boxes.

sections.heading: Privacy Policy That Passes Review
sections.body: Your Privacy Policy must state plainly that you do not sell or share opt-in data. If it mentions "data sharing" without this clarification, your registration can get rejected. Include this language:
bullets: Do not sell or share mobile numbers, SMS consent, or message data
Share only with service providers to operate your SMS program
Include frequency, rates, STOP, and HELP disclosures

sections.heading: Your Sample Messages Matter
sections.body: When you register, you provide sample messages. They need your brand name and STOP/HELP language. Generic placeholders get rejected.

rows.label: ✓ Compliant
rows.value: "Brightside: Appt confirmed Tue 3/12 at 10am. Reply STOP or HELP."

sections.heading: What Gets a Form Rejected
sections.body: Avoid these and you will clear review the first time around.
bullets: One combined checkbox covering all SMS types
Consent implied just by submitting the form
SMS consent hidden only inside Terms or Privacy links
Missing STOP, HELP, business name, or rate disclosures

sections.heading: Pre-Submission Checklist
sections.body: Run through this before you submit. If everything checks out, you are in good shape.
bullets: Business name matches registration, website, and sample messages
Dedicated, optional phone number field on the form
Separate unchecked checkboxes for each message type
Terms and Privacy links present with their own checkbox
Sample messages include brand name and realistic content

sidebar.heading: Required disclosures
sidebar.callout_text: Your Salesmsg team is happy to review your opt-in form before you submit. A two-minute check now can save days of back-and-forth with the carriers.
